Documentation Standard
Answered once, at engagement. These set how strictly the estate is documented, and they are facts, not judgment calls — get them from the representative or counsel. The strictness they produce cannot be lowered later.
Unknown counts as yes. Do not downgrade this on a verbal “probably not” — it needs an answer from the attorney or PR.
Contested Probate already counts as disputed — leave this alone there. Tick it when an ordinary probate turns contested mid-job, so documentation tightens without changing the service type and re-pricing the engagement. Ticking it drops the specialist-appraisal threshold to $500 per item.
Ask the attorney: do you want us to build the inventory, or does your paralegal? This seeds the estimate’s Documentation scope, which prices it; the walkthrough can still override it there. Default to the first until they say otherwise.

Google Integrations

Gmail — HTML Estimate Emails
Lets Email to Client build the estimate as a formatted HTML email with the PDF attached, as a draft in your own Gmail — so it sends from whoever is signed in on this device and lands in their Sent folder. The firm’s client is already filled in — leave it alone unless you are pointing this device at a different Google Workspace. Clearing the box restores the default. This is not a secret; a browser client id is public by design and the authorized origin is what protects it.
Agreement Signatures
Agreements go out through DocuSign. There is nothing to switch on here, and there used to be. The choice was a per-device setting that defaulted to off, so whether a client got a signature request depended on which laptop pressed send — which is exactly what happened on 18 Sep. The credentials live in the Apps Script, one deployment shared by every device, so it is a firm-level fact and is now treated as one.

How each client signs is still chosen per job, on the agreement step of the client’s timeline: Send for signature mails the signing packet through DocuSign, or Send as PDF to sign by hand emails it the old way for a client who would rather print it, or for one you are going to sit down with in person. On a DocuSign job the timeline turns green on its own once both signatures are in, and Record the signed agreement is hidden on that job — a signature typed by hand would disagree with the envelope. Every other job keeps it.
Stripe Payments — nothing to set here
Stripe runs through the same Apps Script as everything else, so there is no second URL to paste. The secret key lives in that script’s Script Properties as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and never on a device — this page is served publicly, so a key typed here would be readable by anyone. Havellin accepts ACH bank transfer only; cards are switched off in the Stripe Dashboard and the app refuses to send a link that is not ACH-only.
Pricing Engine
The Transition Concierge is on site for every crew hour. This is the share of those hours they spend packing, photographing, and handling rather than directing — work that comes out of the same pool the specialists draw from, so it is billed once, on the concierge line. Higher = fewer specialist hours and a shorter job.

This is only the value a fresh estimate starts at. The rate itself is set per estimate, on Build Estimate under the crew counts, because it is a judgement about the property — low on a trophy estate where the concierge is mostly directing, high on a straightforward home editing job where they work the whole day. A saved estimate keeps the rate it was priced under.
Assumed Crew Cost — before anyone is named
Internal only. These drive the margin panel and the walk-away floor — they are never shown to a client and never billed.

A named person always beats these. Anthony, Ashley and every contractor carry their own rate on their own record in the Contractors directory, and that rate is what gets used the moment they are on the job. These four are only the assumption made before a name exists — which at estimate time is normally the whole specialist crew, since you pick a headcount there and name people on the Job Plan once the job is Won. So these price the margin on an estimate; the real rates take over as the crew is staffed.
Raising a cost rate lowers margin and raises the walk-away floor on every fresh estimate. A saved estimate keeps the crew cost it was priced with, so changing these never restates a quote you have already given.

Scoring Reference Guide
Use the same score for Volume and Complexity unless they differ meaningfully. When in doubt, score what you see — don't adjust for what the client tells you.
Volume — How much is in the room?
Score What it looks like
1 Sparse — Nearly empty. Vacation/seasonal property, recently decluttered, or minimal furnishings. Walkways fully clear, minimal closet contents.
2 Light — Below-average volume. Orderly, easy access throughout. Closets manageable. Short-term occupancy or active decluttering already underway.
3 Standard — Normal household accumulation. Fully furnished, closets reasonably full, some storage overflow. Typical long-term primary residence. Default score.
4 Dense — Above-average accumulation. Storage areas overflowing, significant closet/garage volume, multiple hobby or collection areas. Pathways clear but room movement is constrained.
5 Extreme — Floor-to-ceiling accumulation. Obstructed pathways (ICD Level 3+). Hoarder-level density. Requires escalation to Anthony before estimating. Do not use default hours — price separately.
Complexity — How difficult is the handling?
Score What it looks like
1 Simple — Common household items only. No fragile, high-value, or specialty items. Straightforward sort and remove.
2 Moderate — Some fragile items (china, glassware), standard furniture requiring care, basic sorting decisions with a cooperative client or executor.
3 Standard — Mix of fragile, sentimental, and moderately valuable items. Some appraisal coordination expected. Normal family dynamics. Default score.
4 High — Significant art, antiques, jewelry, wine, or collections requiring appraiser coordination. Multiple beneficiaries with competing interests. Documented chain-of-custody required throughout.
5 Specialist — Firearms, cryptocurrency, active business interests, contested probate, biohazard, or multiple high-value categories requiring licensed specialist coordination. Escalate to Anthony immediately.
Remember: Score 3 is the starting point for a normally furnished Palm Beach home. Score up if you see density or complexity above average. Score down for condos, vacation properties, or recently downsized spaces. When Vol and Complexity differ significantly, score each independently — the app handles them separately.
